wire.title: Fire guts Port Alder warehouse; twelve treated for smoke inhalation
paragraphs: A fire tore through a storage warehouse on the Port Alder industrial estate late on Sunday, sending a column of black smoke over the harbour and forcing the closure of two nearby roads.
Twelve people were treated for smoke inhalation after the fire at the Port Alder warehouse, officials said. None of the injuries were described as life-threatening.
At least 40 firefighters were sent to the scene from Port Alder and three neighbouring towns, and the blaze took 6 hours to bring under control.
The warehouse, owned by the logistics firm Brennock Freight, held packaging materials and household goods awaiting shipment to retailers across the region.
Residents within half a mile of the site were told to keep windows and doors closed overnight while crews dampened down hot spots.
Investigators have not yet said what caused the fire. A spokesperson for the regional fire service said an inquiry would begin once the building was declared safe to enter.
Harbour Road and Quay Lane remained closed on Monday morning, and the town council advised drivers to use the coast road instead.
Brennock Freight said in a statement that all of its staff on the night shift had been accounted for and thanked emergency crews for their response.

morrow.title: Port Alder blaze: dozen hurt as warehouse burns
paragraphs: A dozen people needed treatment for breathing in smoke when the Port Alder warehouse caught fire, according to officials, though none were seriously hurt.
At least 40 firefighters were sent to the scene from Port Alder and three neighbouring towns, and the blaze took 6 hours to bring under control.

Morrow Daily understands that the building had passed a fire safety inspection in the spring, though the inspection report has not been published.

day2.title: Port Alder fire: 14 treated, man arrested on suspicion of arson
paragraphs: Police investigating the Port Alder warehouse fire have arrested a 34-year-old man on suspicion of arson, the regional force said on Tuesday.
14 people were treated for smoke inhalation after the fire at the Port Alder warehouse, officials said. None of the injuries were described as life-threatening.
At least 40 firefighters were sent to the scene from Port Alder and three neighbouring towns, and the blaze took 6 hours to bring under control.
The warehouse, owned by the logistics firm Brennock Freight, held packaging materials and household goods awaiting shipment to retailers across the region.
Harbour Road and Quay Lane reopened on Tuesday morning, and the town council advised drivers to use the coast road instead.
Brennock Freight said in a statement that all of its staff on the night shift had been accounted for and thanked emergency crews for their response.
The man was released on bail pending further inquiries and is due to report back to police in November, a force spokesperson added.
